references.text: The priest shall examine the leper and declare him clean or unclean—this is the Mosaic law Jesus refers to when he tells the healed man to show himself to the priest.

Moses' law concerning the cleansing of a leper, including the sacrifices to be brought. Jesus commands the man to bring an offering 'as Moses commanded,' and this passage describes exactly these regulations.
Matthew's parallel account of the healing of the leper, where Jesus also commands him to show himself to the priest and present the gift Moses required, as a testimony to them.
Mark's parallel account of the healing of the leper, where Jesus strictly charges him not to tell anyone, but to go and show himself to the priest and bring the offering Moses prescribed.
Moses' command to carefully follow the priests' instructions regarding leprosy—a part of Mosaic legislation that Jesus refers to.
A later account in Luke where Jesus again commands healed lepers to go and show themselves to the priests, in accordance with Mosaic law.
At the raising of Jairus' daughter, Jesus instructed the parents not to tell anyone what had happened—a similar command for silence as in Luke 5:14.
Jesus commands the people not to tell about the miracle—another example of Jesus' instruction for silence after a healing, parallel to the command in Luke 5:14.
The introduction to the law concerning the day of cleansing for the leper, where the healed person must be brought before the priest—the very legal basis for Jesus' command.
